domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Establish compatible operands
skills.definition: Prepare operands so subtraction can proceed directly by rewriting them into compatible forms, including finding common denominators, converting to equivalent fractions, and normalizing whole numbers or nonstandard mixed numbers.
skills.merge_rationale: S01 and S02 are both preparatory transformations applied before subtraction. In the dossiers, both serve the same problem-solving phase: making operands subtraction-ready. They are diagnostically close because both involve representation change rather than execution of subtraction.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction once operands are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators over a common denominator and subtracting whole and fractional parts separately.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because execution of subtraction is a distinct cognitive operation from preparation, regrouping, simplification, and final formatting.

skills.name: Regroup for subtraction
skills.definition: Borrow or regroup across whole and fractional parts when the fractional part of the minuend is insufficient for subtraction.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because borrowing produces a distinctive error pattern and is not always required. It has strong diagnostic value in mixed-number and whole-minus-fraction items.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the resulting fraction or rewrite zero-valued fractional results into simpler equivalent forms.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification is a finalization skill with its own common student errors and does not always co-occur with recombination.

skills.name: Compose final form
skills.definition: Recombine whole and fractional parts or present the result in its final mixed-number, fraction, or integer form.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final answer composition is distinct from simplification; students may correctly compute parts yet fail to express the final form properly.
